Label: Big Bethel AME Church
Description: Big Bethel African Methodist Episcopal (AME) Church traces its roots back to 1847, with a group of enslaved persons who were part of 'Union Church,' the very first congregation formed in Atlanta. Although Union Church, which eventually disbanded, was established for whites, the original enslaved group that was allowed to worship there remained intact. Whites eventually granted a petition for those enslaved to have their own church and set aside $700 for that purpose. In 1855, 'Bethel Tabernacle' was completed. Indeed, while Big Bethel is often referred to as Atlanta's first Black congregation, it is more accurately recognized as Atlanta's oldest congregation, Black or white.

Our global network, with nearly 2500 members, offers members a space to connect with one another, collaborate on impactful projects, and create change through knowledge sharing and collective action. This includes our Annual Black Sustainability Summit, which connects sustainability practitioners across the globe, and out Black Sustainability Institute, an online learning platform of specialized green courses. Our RBG Impact Fund reinvests a portion of membership dues into member projects. Finally, we run educational workshops with members to share knowledge. Our focus includes everything from sustainable agriculture and alternative energy to environmental justice and alternative economics.

Label: Drawdown Georgia
Description: Drawdown Georgia is a statewide initiative working to catalyze a Georgia beyond carbon. Our road map lays out a vision for scaling Georgia-specific climate solutions in ways that prioritize equity and public health, create jobs, and nurture the natural environment. Our goal is to help Georgians build a new, sustainable future based on our diversity, our ingenuity, and our shared humanity. Drawdown Georgia is a research-based initiative launched in 2020 that was born from a multi-university collaboration, funded by the Ray C. Anderson Foundation. The research was led by Georgia Tech, with partners from Emory University, Georgia State University, and the University of Georgia. The research team released its initial findings in October 2020. That work identified the 20 high-impact climate solutions that put Georgia on a path to advance drawdown'that point in the future when levels of greenhouse gasses in the atmosphere stop climbing and start to steadily decline. With these 20 climate solutions as a roadmap, Drawdown Georgia is bringing together businesses, universities, NGOs, policymakers, and others to join the movement to take us further, faster.

When I was getting into gardening and farming, it was kind of intimidating and I had all this uncertainty about how its done. Theres all this conflicting information from books and online, and once I found people who I could garden with, it just made much more sense to me when I was learning with my hands. [So] to have a space where people can get their hands dirty, to have that place to be able to garden and interact with different plants... because everybody deserves that....[Also] a lot of these plants, we can divide and save seeds from, take cuttings from, and so this can be a source for all these other plants to be propagated and spread out into this eco region...for me is the idea of this being like a mother." Having more places where people can interact, share knowledge about plants, learn to grow their own food and medicine, take seeds and cuttings to propagate at home, and build community and deeper connection to plants is his mission for the space. 'I want my relationship with plants to be deeper than me just trying to keep a large group of them sort of alive enough for me to get harvest. And so I think growing on a smaller scale and encouraging other people to grow their own food and build that relationship with plants is a big goal of mine...it's fun to me to have a smaller pocket garden and to be interacting with people that are trying to grow their own food or grow their own medicine, or even just grow stuff for the birds and bees. Label: Georgia Grown
Description: Georgia Grown is a division of the Georgia Department of Agriculture that helps grow local agribusinesses. Georgia Grown members join a network of certified local producers and benefit from increased exposure to potential customers, suppliers, and partners.

Label: Another Chance Atlanta
Description: We are proud to provide housing and support for Veterans and offer Recovery Support Services to people in recovery and their families. By combining compassionate case management with strong community relationships, we help our neighbors rebuild their lives and maintain long-term stability. Our mission is about housing and empowering the community 'and hope always.
Address: 3700 Wendell Dr SW, Suite 4, Atlanta, GA 30336

Label: White Oak Pastures
Description: Regenerative Livestock Farm. White Oak Pastures is Radically Traditional Farming. Every day, we butcher meat from animals raised in a regenerative manner using humane animal management practices. This is no easy task, but it is our passion. To operate our vertically integrated, zero-waste model, it takes 160+ caring people working together to accomplish a common goal: taking care of our land and our livestock. White Oak Pastures is a Zero-Waste farm. We sell the meats we butcher on our farm to passionate consumers who care about the animals, land and the community. The hides from the cattle we slaughter are dried for pet chew rawhides or tanned and crafted into leather goods. The fat from our cattle is rendered down to create some of the purest tallow products available. The inedible viscera is composted to later be spread on our farm as rich organic matter to fertilize our soil.

Label: Hope House
Description: Transitional community housing offers a supportive environment for individuals re-entering society after incarceration or completing a drug or alcohol rehabilitation program. These programs provide stable housing and a structured framework to help residents rebuild their lives with dignity and purpose.

Label: Mushroom Club of Georgia
Description: The Mushroom Club of Georgia is an educational, social and outdoor-oriented organization. Our mission is to promote the study of all aspects of the fungal world, including foraging and identifying wild mushrooms, cultivating edible and medicinal mushrooms, making art using fungi and exploring the ways fungi interact with our environment. Everyone interested in fungi are welcome to join the club. Mushroom Club of Georgia members are invited on our nature walks to find and identify wild mushrooms, led by experienced club members and expert mycologists. We host classes to teach scientific methods of identifying wild mushrooms. We hold dinners and recipe exchanges, helping members to better enjoy the culinary delights of wild and cultivated mushrooms. We invite members to participate in programs to educate the public about the many benefits of fungi. We also organize classes to teach members how to cultivate edible mushrooms. This is a state chapter of the North American Mycological Association (NAMA), a 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization.

Label: The Investors Academy Inc
Description: The Investors Academy was established in 2015 as a resource to support veterans and parolees Prior to being based at the Resource Center, our Executive Director facilitated pop-up events and programs within communities across SW Atlanta. We rallied a community of volunteers and created a grassroots effort to provide diverse programming. In 2017 we received our 501C3 status and obtained a hub to house our programs. We named this hub The Resource Center as it offers a safe space for the community to obtain resources.

Label: World Centric
Description: We manufacture compostable and reusable foodservice and packaging products and give 25% of our profits to social and environmental organizations to further their work in creating a better world.

Label: Urban Recipe
Description: Urban Recipe ?promotes food security and dignity through intentionally designed community-driven food cooperatives ??prioritizing equitable food access, relationship building, and participation in decision-making. They have several Atlanta-based food co-ops, which offer a bi-weekly distribution of frozen and non-perishable food, produce, and home goods, fostering a supportive community. They also provide short-term food support in the metro-Atlanta area through their Mobile Pantry. Finanly, their Cooperative Pathway Program offers local organizations the needed tools and support to launch food co-ops in their communities.
Address: 970 Jefferson St NW Suite 7, Atlanta, GA 30318

Label: Reynoldstown Farmers Market
Description: This market is small, but mighty. Located at Lang Carson Recreation Center as part of RCIL's Health & Wellness Initiative, the market is within walking distance of our entire neighborhood and just 100 yards off the Beltline. We have a strong sense of community and a deep communication reach with our residents. We host a weekly classes/activities to promote a healthy lifestyle, as well as fresh, local produce for sale. Keep in touch here and on socials to see what's happening each week!
Address: 100 Flat Shoals Ave SE, Atlanta, GA 30316

Label: Ecosystem Farm
Description: Ecosystem Farm is a no-spray upick strawberry farm run by Kirsten Simmons. Ecosystem Farm grows soil microbes that support nutrient dense food without the use of pesticides, herbicides, fungicides or fertilizers.

Label: Providence Missionary Baptist Church
Description: Providence Missionary Baptist Church provides well'balanced bags of uncooked foods weekly for Church and community recipients. The Friday weekly distribution is targeted toward families in need, those suffering from AIDS and the elderly.
Address: 2295 Benjamin E Mays Dr SW, Atlanta, GA 30311

Label: Heaps Pies
Description: Heaps was born out of Jake Harvey's desire to re-create the magic of a New Zealand pie, and to bring a bit of his culture and Wh?nau to the Atlanta community. At Heaps, he combines this food tradition with his love and knowledge of global cuisine. Heaps partners with local purveyors such as Riverview Farms, Southern Cap Mushrooms, Pine Street Market, and Love is Love Farm. Awarded Snail of Approval from Slow Food Atlanta (2025).
Address: 2752 E Ponce de Leon Ave, Suite A1, Atlanta, GA

Description: We are here for you and your family, here at F.A.V.O.R Nothing About Your Family Without Your Family With the assistance of F.A.V.O.R., you will be able to explore and evaluate all possible options available to help your family have a brighter future. Our organization is committed to bridging the gap between communities by inspiring families to strive towards a positive outlook on life.
Address: 798 Rays Road Suite 94, Stone Mountain, GA 30083

Label: Georgia Aquaculture and Aquaponics Network
Description: Led by Fort Valley State University - To promote, develop, and support the aquaculture and aquaponics community in the State of Georgia. To identify and apply best practices that enable innovative, healthy, and sustainable food production systems. To identify, develop, and promote appropriate and scalable technologies for application in the network community. To serve members of the network by developing effective purchasing and marketing systems. Engage, collaborate and cooperate with other established networks and entities that embrace our shared values. Provide information sharing forums, and educational outreach for individual and network communications.

Label: The Spotted Trotter
Description: The Spotted Trotter is a Boutique Charcuterie House and Butcher Shop in Atlanta, GA. It is our passion to always provide our clientele with exquisite balance in flavor, price, and sustainability. All of our ingredients are purveyed with responsibility in mind. We make the food you eat the food you love because it is handled with the utmost respect ' from the farmer that produced it to your dining table. Received renewed Snail of Approval award from Slow Food Atlanta (2025).

Label: New Hope Seventh Day Adventist Church
Description: The New Hope Food Pantry is open to serve the public every 3rd Sunday, 11:00 AM to 1:00 PM.

Label: DaySpring Farms
Description: DaySpring Farms is family owned and operated by Murray and Paula Brett and is powered by their dream to reclaim a better and more sustainable way of life. The 95 acre farm was founded in 2011 and is located just outside of Danielsville, GA in Madison County and is USDA Certified Organic. DaySpring's Mill provides a full line of organic wheat flours and corn products. Our grains are grown, cleaned, and milled fresh on site to achieve the Bretts' goal of offering the most sustainably produced and highest quality product they possibly can and to help provide a healthy and more sustainable way of life for the surrounding community.

Label: Science for Georgia
Description: Science for Georgia is a non-profit that works to ensure Georgia understands, values, and engages with science. We are dedicated to bridging the gap between scientists and the public through training, outreach, and advocating for the responsible use of science in public policy. They run a 'Data for Georgia' program which joins communities, data science students, public health students, and experienced science communicators to tell actionable data stories that communities can use to create change. Some of their interests are related to data on food security and food access. They also run various 'Cimate Survival' trainings, many of which center around growing your own food and composting!

Label: Slow Food Emory
Description: Slow Food Emory is a local campus chapter of the international Slow Food Movement. Our main goal is to advocate 'good, clean, and fair' food in a way that is adaptable and accessible to all Emory students. Slow Food Emory strives to reconnect students to the soil, water, organisms, cultures, and traditions salient to the production of food and establish sustainable communal interactions. Slow Food Emory seeks to invigorate genuine interest in food policy and production, encourage student involvement with the local sustainable food community, and encourage an appreciation for the importance of food in our daily lives. They have been partnering with Retaaza since 2024 to divert leftover produce at Grant Park Farmers Market to their club, where they use it to prepare meals for patients and family members at the Winship Cancer Center.

Label: EcoWomanist Institute Southeast
Description: A nonprofit organization that serves as a "safe and informative space for the EcoWomanist." They support cohorts of Black women farmers.

Label: Power Atlanta Inc.
Description: P.O.W.E.R. Atlanta host a community-based food pantry program that collects and safely stores food and household products for free distribution. We offer essentials such as, non-perishables and dry food, toothbrushes, tooth paste, feminine products, baby diapers/wipes, baby food, soap, and household cleaners to help Fulton County residents in need. If you or someone you know in the local area are in need of these resources we encourage you to come out every Thursday for assistance. Be sure to check our our website, subscribe to our newsletter, and follow us on social media for more support and additional programs.

Label: Market 166 Co-op
Description: Market 166 is a community-rooted cooperative grocery store created by neighbors seeking better, fresher local food options. As an Owner, you invest in the community's wellbeing, vote on key decisions, and help ensure that store profits stay local, benefiting the community rather than out-of-town corporations. We own it, build it, and benefit from it right here at home. "What's unique about our local concept is that it's not just about selling a product. It's about bringing the community together...Right now, you don't have things that connect you, especially with social media'it doesn't necessarily connect you to people in your community. It may connect you to isolated groups, but it doesn't connect you to your neighbor two blocks over. But a grocery store, a community grocery store, could." - Robert Adu-Marfo

The farm is located on 175 acres of pristine creeks, pastures and hardwood forests in Newborn, GA where they specialize in vegetable, fruit, flower and medicinal herb production.

Address: 3726 E Main St, College Park Georgia 30337, United States

Label: Healing Hipster
Description: Healing Hipster is a 1.5 acre urban farm in South Fulton, owned and operated by Jasmine Herndon. She grows food, makes value-added products, and teaches her community how to stay healthy by growing their own food. Her goal is to make growing food approachable. At her farm, she teaches classes and offers $25 Food Bundles, her version of a CSA. Customers can buy bundles at any time without paying in advance, giving them variety and flexibility.
Topics: Urban Agriculture | Value-Added Products | Education Outreach | Herbalism | Nutrition, Health, & Wellness

Label: Ke'nekt Cooperative
Description: The Ke'nekt Cooperative is a caf' in Southwest Atlanta, identifying as a Black-liberated third space. The Ke'nekt was born out of a statistic we've known to be true in Atlanta for a while: large infrastructure projects and economic engines like the Beltline have accelerated not just residential gentrification and displacement, but also the displacement of legacy Black businesses. If there is such a thing as economic genocide, it is happening as we speak, and is being furthered by the economic impacts of a global pandemic that is disproportionately affecting Black folks.. The result is a loss of economic, political, and cultural power for Black communities.The Ke'nekt Cooperative was born to repair and remediate this loss. Through collective action and shared cooperative principles, we are creating an economic empowerment ecosystem that fosters ownership, sustainability, and generational wealth. By prioritizing equitable access to resources, opportunities, and decision-making, we aim to break cycles of economic exclusion and build a thriving, self-sufficient community where prosperity is shared, not concentrated. Our work is driven by the belief that economic justice is the foundation for true empowerment, and together, we are reshaping the landscape of commercial real estate to reflect our values of unity, equity, and resilience.
Address: 1492 Ralph David Abernathy Blvd SW Suite A, Atlanta, GA 30310

Label: Good Roots
Description: Good Roots is a firm that helps farmers and food entrepreneurs grow strong, foundational roots in business. With decades of experience in farming and food systems, we're here to help you get out of the weeds and thrive. Good Roots provides accounting, business consulting, and marketing services.

Label: G-SPAN
Description: The Georgia State Physical Activity and Nutrition initiative (G-SPAN) is working across Georgia to advance health equity and improve well-being through community-driven solutions. Made possible with funding from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, G-SPAN focuses on creating lasting change through policy, systems, and environmental strategies in four priority areas: physcial activity; nutrition; early care and education; and breastfeeding. We collaborate with community members, local partners, and statewide organizations to reduce health disparities, uplift community voices, and share what works. Together, we're building healthier, more equitable communities across Georgia.
Address: Georgia Health Policy Center Eighth Floor, 55 Park Pl NE, Atlanta, GA 30303, USA

Label: James Beard Foundation
Description: James Beard Foundation believes in a vibrant, equitable, and sustainable independent restaurant industry that stands as a cornerstone of American culture, community and economy, and drives towards a better food system. We amplify and recognize, educate and train those committed to excellence ' fostering a deep appreciation among food lovers for the industry's vital contributions to food culture.
Address: 49 West 27th Street, 2nd Floor, New York, NY 10001

Label: Andrew and Walter Young Family
Description: Named in honor of civil rights leaders and Atlanta icons Ambassador Andrew Young and Dr. Walter Young, the Andrew & Walter Young Family YMCA was founded in 1959 and was formerly known as the Southwest Y. As one of the earliest Ys in Atlanta, the Young Family Y has been serving the communities of East Point, College Park, Hapeville and West End for more than 60 years through programs focused on youth development, healthy living and social responsibility.

Label: Bon Appetit Management Company
Description: Bon Appetit is an on-site restaurant company offering full food-service management to corporations, universities, museums, and venues. They have developed a "Farm to Fork" purchasing program, requiring their chefs to buy at least 20% of their ingredients from small farmers, producers, and fishermen within 150 miles of their kitchens.

Label: Lifecycle Building Center
Description: Lifecycle Building Center is a nonprofit that captures building materials from the waste stream and directs them back into the community through reuse. Their warehouse is open to the public to purchase reclaimed building materials at a low cost - this can include anything from wood, metal, and pallets to sinks, fridges, lighting fixtures, and more! Additionally, ?thorugh LBC's Nonprofit Material MATCH Program, they donate free building materials to federally registered nonprofits, schools, community groups and houses of faith. This is a great option for community gardens and local nonprofit farms to acquire free building materials, such as wood or metal for raised beds, or cold storage items! LBC also runs various events. Through Do-It-Yourself Classes, Home Performance Workshops, fundraisers and networking events, attendees can engage with LBC's staff, board and other supporters to explore deeper collaboration opportunities, and connect with like-minded philanthropists, community representatives and corporate leaders in the design, construction and real estate sectors.

Label: Mother Clyde Memorial West End Garden Urban Pepper Farm
Oakhurst Community Garden
Description: Beautiful Oakhurst Garden was the first garden in the Wylde Center family. It was founded in 1997 as a community garden that focused on environmental education. Since then, the garden has seen a lot of change, most recently with large-scale improvements to the garden and the building on the property. Because it was the first garden, people often refer to Oakhurst Garden as Wylde Center.

Label: The Giving Tree Garden (South Dekalb YMCA)
Doghead Farm
Description: Doghead Farm is a non-profit urban farm in the West Atlanta neighborhood of Mozley Park. We transform an otherwise neglected plot of land, formerly overrun by kudzu, into a productive, sustainable, and beautiful place where we can teach and serve the community, as well as fight food insecurity. We are a volunteer-based organization and utilize permaculture techniques to achieve our goal. We grow literal tons of vegetables each year, which are then donated to Atlanta's homeless and hungry populations.
Topics: Nutrition, Health, & Wellness | Urban Agriculture | Land Access

Label: Blackbird Farm
Description: Blackbird Farm is located 30 minutes south of Atlanta. We have a mission to farm in a way that is good for the environment, good for people, and good for business. We grow our plants in a deep-water culture aquaponics system. This system is a symbiotic relationship between our fish and our plants. The fish fertilize the plants and the plants filter the water, providing the fish with a clean place to live. The water is constantly recirculating, which helps us to conserve our water. In the last year, we have been able to expand our offerings beyond our greens to include farm stays, tours, and an event venue.

Label: Cheffrey's Kitchen
Description: After working at one of Osaka's most prestigious restaurants for over 10 years, Chef Kiyoka was selected by the Japanese Consulate General in Atlanta to become their official chef. She yearned to find local vegetables, meat, and fish like she had access to in Japan. Now via Cheffrey's Kitchen, Chef Kiyoka wants the community to experience the joining of Japanese cuisine with Atlanta's locally grown produce. Her focus is to use quality seasonal ingredients, through future collaboration with local Georgia organic farms, to create an edible artistic landscape within each hand-crafted bento box. Her vision comes to life through making exquisite, accessible, and affordable bento boxes. They host chef pop-ups at East Atlanta Village Farmers Market every Thursday. Awarded Snail of Approval from Slow Food Atlanta (2025).

Label: Park Pride
Description: Park Pride is working in Atlanta's parks ecosystem at every level'by improving neighborhood parks, creating community parks advocates, and connecting grassroots leaders, funders, and government partners'so that all Atlantans can have access to a great park. Park Pride provides Small Change Grants, volunteer project support, compost, networking, and leadership workshops to associated community gardens in Atlanta.
Contact: Ellen Bruenderman Director of Community Services ellen@parkpride.org (502) 938-1225

Label: Andrews Angels In Mission
Description: Located inside of Faith and Grace Lutheran Church in Decatur, GA our mission is "fighting hunger and feeding the souls we serve". We don't just hand you a random box of food that you may or may not eat. We let you choose from a list of inventory so you get what you want and it reduces food waste. We also participate in the TEFAP program.

Label: Operation D.E.F.R.O.S.T.
Description: Operation D.E.F.R.O.S.T. is a 501(c)3 nonprofit organization whose purpose is to aid families who reside in underserved and underrepresented communities of metro-Atlanta, by bridging economic and societal gaps that they undergo. We accomplish this through our food pantry, clothing drives, back to school events, holiday initiatives, and other outreach endeavors. D.E.F.R.O.S.T. is an acronym that stands for the seven principals in which we operate from: Discipline Energy Focus Respect Omnipotence Serenity and Trust. Through both our initiatives and disciplines, we strive to mitigate economic vulnerability across metro-Atlanta

Label: Mission Agape
Description: Our Mission is to provide support and resources to homeless individuals and families at risk of homelessness, with the ultimate goal of helping to empower the homeless to live fulfilling and self-sufficient lives.

Label: Master Gardener Volunteers of Cobb County
Description: Master Gardener Volunteers Of Cobb County Assist The Local Community Through 16 Community and Demonstration Gardens throughout Cobb County
Address: 678 South Cobb Drive Suite 200 Marietta, GA 30060

Label: Certified Naturally Grown
Description: Certified Naturally Grown (CNG) offers peer-review certification to farmers and beekeepers producing food, flowers, and fiber for their local communities by working in harmony with nature, without relying on synthetic chemicals or GMOs. Our standards are based on the highest ideals of the organic movement. Our approach is based on transparency, direct relationships and a firm belief in our ability to create something uniquely valuable by working together.

Label: Gangstas to Growers
Description: Gangstas to Growers (G2G) was founded with a vision to transform lives and communities through sustainable agriculture. Established in 2016, our social enterprise emerged from the recognition that many at-risk and formerly incarcerated youth face significant barriers to employment and empowerment. We believe that everyone deserves a second chance and the opportunity to thrive. Our current projects include hands-on training in seeding, growing, harvesting, and even product creation. A highlight of our offerings is the Sweet Sol hot sauce, made from ingredients grown and harvested by our youth. This product not only infuses flavor into your meals but also directly supports our program and the young people involved.

Label: Think Green Inc.
Description: Think Green Inc is an environmental education non-profit, founded by Khari Diop. We are committed to: Connecting people to planet through technology and enhancing the natural environment through design. We are a community benefit organization on a mission; honoring the mandate to preserve and protect planet earth. We practice thoughtful, vigilant stewardship and purposeful, creative restoration. We cultivate vibrance and redefine greenspace while creating, transforming and renewing environments. Think Green manages the Community Compost Learning Lab at the Truly Living Well Center for Natural Urban Agriculture and co-leads the Westside Compost Project.

Label: EBC Cares
Description: EBC Cares is dedicated to transforming lives and communities through service, education, and support. We partner with local organizations to address the diverse needs of our neighborhoods, empowering individuals and creating lasting change. ounded as an outreach ministry of Elizabeth Baptist Church, EBC Cares was born out of a desire to serve our community and respond to God's call to make a tangible difference in the lives of those around us. From our humble beginnings, we've grown into an organization dedicated to addressing the most pressing needs in our neighborhoods, offering everything from education scholarships to food distribution and community development projects. As of 2025, impact includes: 60K Meals Distributed 358 Tax Returns Filed 17.5K Scholarships Awarded

Label: Rag & Frass Farm
Description: Rag & Frass Farm is a small-scale farm in Georgia that is dedicated to regenerative farming practices and building healthy, living soil. We grow a diverse range of seasonal vegetables and herbs with a deep appreciation for the ecological processes that support our work. Our mission is to provide high-quality, wholesome food while creating a farm that is in harmony with the natural world.

Label: Leaven Kitchen
Description: Leaven is a collaborative kitchen in Decatur, GA that provides inclusive, flexible, and affordable shared use commercial kitchen space to growing food businesses. We equip our members with 13 work stations in 6 different configurations to be able to help any food or drink business rise and transform. Along with our kitchen, we rent speciality equipment, offer ample dry storage, walk-in refrigerator and freezer, coworking office space, and bathrooms with lockers and showers so that Leaven can be your one-stop-shop for growing your business. We are committed to your growth and the growth of your business. We are able to connect you with consultants and resources to get the licensing, marketing, packaging, delivery and business help needed to empower your business to grow. This space can also be rented out for photo shoots, YouTube videos, cooking classes, pop up events, community dinners, and product tasting.

Label: Sustainable Community Solutions
Description: Sustainable Community Solutions is a management consulting firm that specializes in sustainable solutions. Unlike traditional consulting firms, we have a uniquely diverse BIPOC network to equitably foster sustainable development, focusing on communities of African descent. We focus on strategry (e.g., program development, project management, community engagement); guidance (design, program management); and education (workforce development, community-based knolwedge translation). In Atlanta, we've worked on projects with: HABESHA, Inc.; Clean Energy Atlanta; the Nature Conservancy and Atlanta's equity index.
Address: 2414 Herring Road SW Suite 42734, Atlanta, GA 30311

Label: Honey Next Door
Description: Honey Next Door keeps bees in local Atlanta neighborhoods to provide hyperlocal honey products and to keep a healthy population of honeybees in the urban ecosystem. We own and manage beehives in Buckhead, Candler Park, Oakhurst, Druid Hills, Inman Park, Virginia Highlands, Brookhaven, Morningside, Pittsburgh, Sandy Springs, East Atlanta Village, Grant Park and Decatur. We sell chemical-free bee products like honey, soap, beeswax candles, and lip balms. We plan to include products like liquid soaps and lotions to the product line soon.

Label: Candler Park Market
Description: We proudly source as much of our produce seasonally from small local farms or regional vendors when possible. We carry a large selection of organic and natural groceries. We believe it is important to be able to find the same quality products free of artificial ingredients and fillers at your neighborhood market as it is at the big box store. That's why we carry a full range of Natural and Organic goods.

Label: Community Foundation for Greater Atlanta
Description: The Community Foundation for Greater Atlanta works with ' and for ' our community. We nurture community voices in South Cobb, South Fulton and Thomasville supporting residents living in those areas. Each of these communities is dramatically different and will require a partnership with residents to develop a neighborhood strategy, both to achieve that voice and to gain consideration in the decision-making process from state and local political representatives.
Address: 191 Peachtree Street NE Suite 1000 Atlanta, GA 30303

Label: Jesse Hill Market
Description: Jesse Hill Market is home to our Food as Medicine program, an innovative program offering all members of the Grady community ' patients, families, employees, visitors, and neighbors ' access to healthy, affordable food in partnership with the Atlanta Community Food Bank and Open Hand Atlanta. Located just outside Grady's main entrance in the Butler Parking Deck, Jesse Hill Market is a public caf' offering a range of healthy items. Purchase nutritious, affordable prepared meals, grab-and-go entrees and sides, and local, fresh produce, at the first retail location of Atlanta's own Good Measure Meals.

Label: Southern Elderberry, Sauce & Pickle Co.
Description: The Southern Sauce Co. offers regional sauces crafted locally in Cumming, Georgia. What began as a family recipe, turned flagship sauce has become a passion for all things BBQ that we are thrilled to share with you. Be sure to try our other sauces, rubs and pickles!

Label: Blessed Divas Corporation
Description: Blessed Divas was founded to empower women to lead lives rooted in service, purpose, and community impact. Our mission is to unite women through hands-on volunteerism and frontline service, offering support where it is needed most. We are dedicated to feeding the hungry, supporting seniors through essential home repairs, organizing community clean-ups, and assisting women and children in local day centers and shelters. While Blessed Divas is a women-driven initiative, we proudly welcome the support and involvement of men and children. We believe that creating meaningful change requires the collective effort of all individuals, regardless of age or gender, working together in service to others.

Label: Concrete Jungle
Description: Concrete Jungle strives to ensure neighbors have access to fresh produce. They rescue fresh fruits and vegetables and donate them to local food banks and shelters. Concrete Jungle also harvests produce from around Atlanta and on their urban farm, Doghead Farm, and distributes the harvests to food banks and shelters.

Label: Atlanta Hospital Hospitality House
Description: Atlanta Hospital Hospitality House (AHHH), established in 1980 in Druid Hills, provided low-cost, "home-away-from-home" lodging for patients and families facing medical crises. The facility offered private rooms, shared kitchens, and support services, serving over 140,000 nights for those receiving care at nearby Atlanta hospitals.

Label: Our Giving Garden
Description: the Giving Garden has donated over 10,000 lbs of organic produce and 12,000 eggs to the Sweetwater Mission Food Pantry. In addition to the Sweetwater Mission, the Garden has also been responsible for gathering donations such as other food items, books, and coats for families in need across the community.
Address: 79 Cooper Lake Rd SE, Mableton, GA 30126

Label: Gaia Gardens
Description: Gaia Gardens is a quintessential, well-constructed and thoughtful meditation on how an organic, diversified production farm sits in the context of an urban community and neighborhood while giving respective representation of the life of the farm, woodland, and pond areas with its boundaries. Essentially, it harbors an oasis of plants, animals, insects, and microorganisms giving weight to the idea that biodiversity is the masterplan for success on Planet Earth.

Label: McMullan Family Farm
Description: McMullan Family Farm is a multi-generational farm that has been providing high-quality products to the community for years. We are committed to traditional farming practices and a deep sense of stewardship for the land we call home. Our mission is to provide our customers with a product that is a true reflection of our family's heritage.

Label: First Presbyterian Church of Atlanta
Description: Founded in 1848, First Presbyterian Church of Atlanta is located at the corner of Peachtree and 16th Streets, next to the Woodruff Arts Center. We are an urban church known for being a leader in worship, spiritual formation, service, community relationships, and the arts. Many families who have helped build this city have been and are members of FPC and the church has celebrated some notable milestones. FPC continues to build on these traditions as we look forward to our 175th Anniversary in 2023.

Label: Mt. Moriah Baptist Church
Address: 200 Joseph E Lowery Blvd SW, Atlanta, GA 30314

Label: Mad Agriculture
Description: Mad Agriculture helps farmers thrive in regenerative organic agriculture. We meet farmers where they're at in their journey as they transition to regenerative agricultural models. They are based in Colorado with a national focus. We support farmers through our four branches: >Mad Capital, providing the most flexible, transparent, and customized financing built exclusively for organic, regenerative, and transitioning farmers. >Mad Lands, providing land and business planning, working directly with the stewards at the heart of the regenerative revolution to build strategies and opportunities for farm businesses, to understand impact and to advance the capacity of regenerative agriculture to feed people while restoring ecosystems. >Mad Markets, innovating marketplace solutions to drive regenerative agriculture >Mad Revolution, weaving diverse forms of art, spirituality, science, and policy to amplify farmer stories, showcase the vitality of regeneration, and invite others to join the movement. They also offer educational resources, such as cirriculum in regenerative agriculture, consulting options, and in-person/online webinars.

Label: Atlanta Utility Works

Description: The Conservation Fund is a national funder that was founded on the idea that environmental protection and economic vitality are mutually reinforcing strategies that make our society stronger. They are twin pillars of a national strategy: economic growth without environmental protection is unsustainable, and environmental protection without economic growth is equally unsustainable. For more than 40 years, The Conservation Fund has been buying at-risk land with high conservation value to protect it from degradation, putting protections in place to ensure it is managed for environmental, economic, and human gain before finding long-term owners. We have worked across all 50 states to conserve more than 9 million acres of irreplaceable American landscapes ' protecting habitat for countless species, supporting millions of jobs, and providing communities across the country with better quality of life. This critical work uniquely positions The Conservation Fund to tackle some of our country's greatest challenges ' from climate solutions, to wildlife protection, to rural economic development, and even access to fresh and healthy food. Our work in conservation is about more than protecting special places, it's also about ensuring that those places will always be healthy, vibrant, and productive contributors to a large and resilient society. 'The Conservation Fund has experts in land acquisition, particularly in navigating its complexity. They step in to acquire at-risk land on behalf of long-term conservation steward partners who may not be able to move quickly enough on their own. The Conservation Fund acts as the acquisition partner, purchasing at-risk lands and then creating a pathway for the conservation partner to eventually buy the land from them" - Justin Nickelson (The Conservation Fund, Georgia) In Atlanta and more broadly across Georgia, the Conservation Fund has supported a number of projects to protect land and green space for the public and incraease land access for farmers. The Conservation Fund works on behalf of city and county partners to purchase land for parks, greenspaces, and trails that will be permanently protected for public use and environmental sustainability, parifcularly through their 'Parks with a Purpose' program in Atlanta (more detail here: https://www.conservationfund.org/our-impact/projects/parks-with-purpose-in-atlanta/). For example, in Atlanta, the Conservation Fund has helped to acquire land for the Browns Mill Food Forest, as well as for the Lake Charlotte Nature Preserve in Southeast Atlanta (216-acres of forested land that would become one of Atlanta's largest protected forests). Read more about the Conservation Fund's work in Atlanta here: https://saportareport.com/the-conservation-fund-making-conservation-work-across-america-and-here-in-atlanta/thought-leadership/the-conservation-fund/ The Conservation Fund is also helping to increase land access for farmers in Georgia, paricularly in the 23 counties surrounding Atlanta, GA. Through the Working Farms Fund Initiative, we secure farmland on the edge of major metro areas and match that farmland to the ideal farmer who leases and stewards the land until TCF protects it forever with an agricultural conservation easement. This is done through a 'Buy-Support-Protect-Sell model', where ultimately the farmer will buy the land back from TCF. Permanently protecting the farm means the land is more affordable for new and growing farm businesses, while keeping it a farm forever. Georgia farms supported by this program include Love is Love Cooperative Farm, Atlanta Harvest, as well as the Rockdale Co-Farm run by the Global Growers Network, among others. Learn more here: https://www.conservationfund.org/our-priorities/working-lands/working-farms/

Description: UGA's Value-addition Institute for Business Expansion (VIBE) is a new center for rural food business assistance and resources headed by professors from the Department of Food Science and Technology in the College of Agricultural and Environmental Sciences (CAES) and the Department of Nutritional Sciences in the College of Family and Consumer Sciences (FACS). VIBE will bring value-added markets to rural parts of Georgia, providing farmers with resources through education and financial assistance to help them move from fresh packing to value-added processing. UGA's multidisciplinary team will travel to meet people for personalized support and to host workshops across the state. 'Farmers using this program would be able to use some of the crops that might not have been suitable for fresh harvest and sale, which would eliminate food waste and provide an additional revenue stream for themselves,' said Kaitlyn Casulli, an assistant professor of food science and technology. VIBE is funded by a $1.5 million grant from the United States Department of Agriculture's Agriculture Innovation Center, a national program that establishes and operates centers that provide aid to agricultural producers seeking to engage in developing and marketing value-added agricultural products. *VIBE is now available to provide one-on-one technical support and workshop offerings on product and process development to help rural farmers and entrepreneurs start food businesses. For more information and to make inquiries, contact Kevin Mis Solval (kmissolval@uga.edu) or Carla Schwan (cls05907@uga.edu).

Label: Carver Neighborhood Market
Description: If you talk with seniors who lived in South Atlanta their whole life, you'll hear stories of a time when 4, yes four, groceries stores served the community of South Atlanta. One only had to walk a few blocks to get the food they needed to survive. Fast forward a few decades and the stores of yesteryear are gone. Small grocery stores were replaced by supermarkets across the county. But too often these new supermarkets were located miles from neighborhoods like South Atlanta. The old stores have had their buildings occupied by other stores. Little Bear, seen here, replaced the Colonial Grocery of the 1950's. Little Bear is not a place where one chooses to go buy their groceries. The corner before Community Grounds and Carver Market! The corner before Community Grounds and Carver Market! In early 2014, we embarked on a fact finding mission in regards to lurring a grocery store to South Atlanta. We found two things: 1) People spend a lot of money on food in our neighborhood, and 2) The amount spent on groceries was not enough for a large national chain to come into our neighborhood anytime soon. While South Atlanta may have had 4 grocery stores at one point, all 4 of them probably could have fit into the frozen food section of a enormous supermarket. We knew by working in South Atlanta since 2001 that access to food was a huge issue. We believe that solving the issue of food access for South Atlantans is critical to returning health and vitality to our community. And so, we started our journey of opening the Carver Neighborhood Market.
